title: drive-ui UI map
description: The map a test case points into: which screens exist, which control is where, and what each control does below the UI. Three files, one record kind each — screens.json, edges.json, effects.json — plus meta.json, which carries provenance AND this product's own vocabulary for layers and timings. A record carries no `t` discriminator: the file it lives in says what it is, so the two cannot disagree. Point a file at the matching definition with "$ref", or validate with `node query.mjs check`, which also enforces the rules a shape cannot express (an edge pointing at a screen that does not exist, an effect hanging off a control that was renamed, an effect using a layer or timing meta.json never declared).

seen.description: live = driven in a real browser and observed; trust it. src = read from frontend source and never watched render; verify on first use, then flip it. Never delete a record to tidy up — a wrong record is evidence.

meta.description: meta.json: where this map came from, and the words this product uses for what it touches. The engine ships no stack vocabulary of its own — declare yours here and `check` holds every effect to it.

fe_commit.description: Frontend commit the map was recorded against.

layers.description: The layers below the UI this product can touch, in the order a QC sheet lists them. Declaring any replaces the engine's default of `sql` alone, so list sql too when you use it.

key.description: The key an effect uses inside `layers` — sql, queue, directory, blob, mail, whatever this stack has.

label.description: What to print. Defaults to the key.

describe.description: How to say one entry, as segments each holding one ${field} of that entry: ["${table}", " (${cols})"]. A segment whose field is absent disappears, so one template covers a full and a bare entry. Without it an entry prints as raw JSON.

timings.description: When an action is finished. The engine assumes `sync` alone; declare every other word an effect may use, or check reports it as undeclared.

name.description: The word an effect's timing uses. `sync` = done when the response returns.

layer.description: The layer key an effect with this timing MUST name: deferred work that does not say what finishes it sends a QC engineer to watch nothing.

note.description: The sentence plan.mjs prints above such a step — what makes this timing a trap, and how to verify it instead of waiting.

id.description: Stable key. Steps say `screen: "<id>"` and edges say `from: "<id>"`.

name.description: What the screen calls itself on screen.

url.description: Route, if it has one. A node with no url is a dialog, wizard tab or row menu — reached by clicking, not by navigating. `{param}` marks a templated segment.

module.description: Frontend module, bundle or feature area it belongs to.

admin.description: Reachable only by an account holding an administrator role.

dead.description: The navigation offers it but no router registers it. Deep-linking renders a fallback screen while keeping the URL, so a case that goes here believes it is somewhere it is not.

stub.description: Placeholder component — there is no UI to drive.

traced.description: A promise that every commit action on this screen has an effect record. It is what lets `query.mjs layers` print “—” (proven untouched) instead of “?” (nobody looked).

reachable.description: Observed reachable in the crawled environment. An ENVIRONMENT fact, not a product fact: routes can come from a per-environment menu payload, so re-crawl rather than inherit it.

note.description: Whatever misleads people about this screen — timing traps, what the rows really are, which shell it belongs to.

from.description: Screen id this control sits on.

via.description: Its label. `from/via` is the key a case step and an effect both address it by, and it is unique across the map.

kind.description: button, link, tab, combobox, textbox, rowmenu, menuitem, icon …

selector.description: The Playwright locator, defined HERE and nowhere else — correcting it fixes every case that walks through this control. "UNKNOWN" means it was never captured and any case naming it will be refused.

options.description: For a combobox: the choices it offers.

opens.description: screen = navigates elsewhere; dialog = modal; panel = inline/side panel; inline = acts in place, no new surface; external = leaves the app; none = no surface change.

to.description: Destination node id, or null when nothing new opens.

required.description: An input that must be filled before the commit control enables.

destructive.description: Deletes or hard-changes real data. Emitted commented-out by plan.mjs, and a case using it needs --force-destructive.

note.description: The trap. Why this selector and not the obvious one, what the label really matches, what a click here silently fails to do.

on.description: The `<screen>/<via>` of the control this describes. Unique — one effect per control.

api.description: The call it makes. Absent when backend is "none".

backend.description: Which deployable serves it — your own names, plus the reserved "none" for a control that calls nothing. Verify it with an `api` step in a case rather than by grepping source.

auth.description: The authorization attribute on the controller action.

src.description: file:line → file:line, frontend through to backend. `query.mjs verify` resolves these and flags any whose file has changed.

timing.description: When it is finished: `sync` (done when the response returns), or any timing meta.json declares. An undeclared word is a check finding.

partial.description: A hop could not be traced. The gap belongs in the QC sheet's Open questions.

persistedBy.description: For a backend:"none" control whose input is written later by another action — names that action.

layers.description: What it touches below the UI, keyed by a layer meta.json declares. OMIT a layer, never empty-array it: an absent key claims “does not touch that layer” and prints “—”, while an untraced control prints “?”. Conflating them is how a QC engineer stops checking something that does happen. Every entry needs its own src — a table name without a file:line is a guess, and worse than a missing one because someone will query it and pass.
